# Where this session starts

## What session 02 handed over

A discharge you can place in time --- when it broke down, what the coils did,
and a vacuum field you have checked against the magnetics.

This session asks what the plasma settled *into*, and whether the stored answer
is really an answer.

::: {.notes}
[2 min]

NARRATE:
Name the prerequisite. Session 02 ended with a field and a breakdown time;
session 03 begins after the current has ramped and the plasma has found a shape.

The session's posture is unusual and worth flagging early: it does not take the
reconstruction on trust. It measures how well the stored equilibrium satisfies
its own governing equation.

TRANSITION:
And that equation is the one thing everything else rests on.
:::

# The equation

## The equation everything rests on

$$\Delta^{*}\psi = -\mu_{0}R^{2}p'(\psi) - FF'(\psi)$$

Flux surfaces are its contours; $p'$ and $FF'$ carry pressure and current.

::: {.notes}
[5 min]

NARRATE:
Read the equation as a statement about force balance collapsing, under
axisymmetry, to one scalar equation for $\psi$. Everything else follows from
$\psi$: the surfaces are its contours, the field is its gradient.

Two free functions, $p'$ and $FF'$. That is what makes reconstruction possible
and also what makes it under-determined.

WARN:
Background the course never defines and this session then uses. Supply it here:

- **separatrix** — the last closed flux surface; outside it, field lines strike
  a wall. Session 01 called it "the boundary of the confined plasma" without
  ever linking the two words.
- **$q$** and **$q_{95}$** — $q$ is the field-line pitch, toroidal turns per
  poloidal turn; $q_{95}$ is its value on the surface enclosing 95% of the flux,
  used because $q$ diverges at a separatrix.
- **$\beta$** — plasma pressure over magnetic pressure, the efficiency of the
  confinement. Toroidal, poloidal and normalised betas are different numbers;
  VAFT displays $\beta_t$ as a percent and the others plain.
- **$\ell_i$** — internal inductance, how peaked the current profile is.

The session's overview promises to "vary shape, beta and internal inductance".
Two of those three have never been defined anywhere in the course.

TRANSITION:
Two codes answer two different questions about this equation.
:::

## Two codes, two questions

- **EFIT reconstructs** --- free boundary, from magnetics.
  *What was the plasma doing?*
- **CHEASE forward-models** --- fixed boundary, from profiles.
  *What do these inputs imply?*

::: {.notes}
[4 min]

NARRATE:
The distinction students most often blur. EFIT is given measurements and finds
the equilibrium most consistent with them; its answer is only as good as the
diagnostics constrain it. CHEASE is given a boundary and two profiles and solves
to numerical precision; it cannot tell you about a discharge it was not given.

Free versus fixed boundary is the concrete difference: EFIT's grid extends past
the plasma to the coils because the boundary is part of the answer. CHEASE works
only inside a boundary you hand it.

WARN:
That difference matters when the session measures the residual of both. Outside
the separatrix $\psi$ folds back near the coils, so a residual computed over the
whole grid says something confident and wrong. Mask on the plasma.

TRANSITION:
And a stored equilibrium carries less than you might expect.
:::

# What is stored, and what is not

## What a g-file does not carry

Six profiles are stored. Volume, shape, $\beta$ and $\ell_i$ are **derived**.

A refused plot is often an underived quantity, not a missing measurement.

::: {.notes}
[3 min]

NARRATE:
This is the session's transferable habit, and it recurs in session 04 inverted.
A g-file is a compact format: $\psi$ on a grid plus six one-dimensional
profiles. Everything else a physicist quotes about an equilibrium is computed
from those.

So when VAFT refuses to plot $\beta_N$, the question to ask is not "does this
shot lack it" but "has anything derived it yet".

WARN:
Conventions bite here. $\beta_p$ names three different quantities in common use,
differing by up to 26% at VEST's aspect ratio, and $\ell_i$ has at least three
definitions. VAFT states which it computes; a number quoted without its
convention is not a number.

TRANSITION:
Which brings up the convention that governs all of this.
:::

## The convention you will meet next

VAFT works internally in **COCOS 11** --- the convention the IMAS Data
Dictionary mandates.

Poloidal flux in full weber, not weber per radian.

::: {.notes}
[3 min]

NARRATE:
COCOS is not mentioned anywhere in this course's notebooks, and it is the first
thing that will confuse a reader who leaves the tutorial for the library. Spend
three minutes.

Sixteen conventions exist [@sauter2013cocos]. They differ in the orientation of
the toroidal and poloidal coordinates, the sign of the poloidal flux, and
whether that flux is divided by $2\pi$. Equilibrium quantities are only
comparable between codes once the index is known.

The practical consequence for this course: EFIT g-files are usually COCOS 1–8,
which store $\psi$ per radian; the Data Dictionary and VAFT's Green's functions
use full weber. A factor of $2\pi$ between them is the single most common
equilibrium bug.

WARN:
Do not tell students to "just multiply by $2\pi$". The conversion carries both
the $2\pi$ and an orientation sign, and applying only the first leaves the field
inverted for half the indices.
:::

## Session workflow

flux map $\rightarrow$ derived 0-D parameters $\rightarrow$ coordinates

$\rightarrow$ camera overlay $\rightarrow$ Grad--Shafranov residual
$\rightarrow$ CHEASE refinement

::: {.notes}
[1 min]

NARRATE:
Point at each step. Note that "coordinates" is a real step, not bookkeeping: a
profile without its radial coordinate is not a physics claim.
:::

## Practice goal: vary the equilibrium

Change the shape, the pressure, the current peaking --- and watch which derived
quantities move.

::: {.notes}
[1 min]

NARRATE:
The exercise is forward modelling, which is only possible because CHEASE takes
inputs rather than measurements. Connect it back to the two-codes slide.
:::
